P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes. Under the CBRT Invisible Transactions Circular of 18 May 2026 (which replaced the 2000/YB-4 circular), residents may freely dispose of foreign currency received from non-residents for services provided in Türkiye or abroad. They may sell it freely to banks, authorised institutions or PTT, or keep it in FX accounts. If such currency is sold to a bank, the bank must sell at least 35% of it on to the CBRT. This is a bank-level rule: the individual is paid in full in lira. The 180-day repatriation duty and the 35% sale rule (Temporary Art. 4, to 31/01/2027) in the CBRT Export Circular apply to export proceeds tied to customs declarations (İBKB/DAB), i.e. goods exports.

The GİB guide on the 20/B content-creator exemption also confirms that foreign-currency proceeds may be paid into the dedicated account; withholding is computed on the lira value at the transfer date.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Generally yes, for tax purposes. Under VUK 213 Art. 153, traders, craftsmen and self-employed professionals (serbest meslek erbabı) must notify the tax office that they have started work. For individuals this is due within 10 days of starting (Art. 168). EXCEPTION, GVK Art. 20/B: social content creators, people selling online courses, data-processing or product-promotion services via online platforms, and mobile-app developers selling through app stores do not keep books or issue invoices. Instead they get an 'İstisna Belgesi' (exemption certificate) from their tax office, which they can apply for online through Dijital Vergi Dairesi. They then collect all revenue through a dedicated Turkish bank account, where the bank withholds 15%. Selling online from your own site or app also requires registering in the Ministry of Trade's ETBİS before starting; sales only via domestic marketplaces are exempt.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: For Turkish citizens the 11-digit T.C. kimlik numarası (national ID number) IS the tax ID. Tax offices have used it as such since 1 July 2006, and it goes in the VKN field of documents. Legal entities use a separate VKN. Tax-office services (Dijital Vergi Dairesi) are accessed with the T.C. ID number and an e-Devlet password.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents (domicile in Türkiye, or more than 6 continuous months in a calendar year) are taxed on worldwide income (GVK Arts. 3-4). The 2026 progressive scale for non-wage income is 15% up to TL 190,000, then 20%, 27%, 35% and 40% above TL 5,300,000. Special regimes: (a) GVK 20/B: income of content creators, platform-based online services and app-store app developers is exempt from income tax, with the bank withholding 15% as a FINAL tax on revenue paid into the dedicated account. This holds while yearly 20/B earnings stay under the 4th-bracket amount (TL 5,300,000 for 2026); above it, all of it is declared. (b) GVK 89/13: 80% of the profit from listed services (architecture, engineering, design, software, data processing and others) provided in Türkiye to non-residents and used exclusively abroad is deductible. This requires an invoice to the foreign customer and the whole profit transferred to Türkiye by the annual return deadline.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: The standard KDV rate is 20% (Presidential Decision 7346, in force 10/07/2023), with reduced rates of 10% and 1%. There is no turnover registration threshold. KDV liability comes with tax registration, but services performed for customers abroad are exempt (KDV Art. 11/1-a). The conditions are that the service is performed for a customer abroad and used abroad (Art. 12/2). Supplies whose income is taxed under GVK 20/B are KDV-exempt under Art. 17/4-a.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698 (KVKK) applies. Personal data may not be processed without explicit consent unless a statutory ground in Art. 5(2) applies, such as performance of a contract. Cross-border transfers need an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards. A standard contract must be notified to the Authority within 5 business days of signing (Art. 9(5), as amended in 2024). VERBIS (data controller registry) registration: controllers with fewer than 50 employees and a balance sheet under TL 100 million are exempt, unless their main activity is processing special-category data (Board Decision 2018/87 as amended by 2025/1572). Controllers that do not keep balance-sheet books (e.g. most sole traders) are judged on employee count only.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Law 6502 on Consumer Protection, Art. 48: for distance contracts, the consumer has 14 days to withdraw without giving reasons. The seller must give pre-contract information and bears the burden of proving it did. Under the Distance Contracts Regulation (Art. 15(1)(ğ)), the right of withdrawal does not apply to services performed instantly in electronic form or intangible goods delivered instantly. The seller must prove that electronically delivered intangible goods or services were free of defects. Law 6563 on E-Commerce requires pre-order information and order confirmation. Sellers with their own site or app, or selling through a foreign platform, must register in ETBİS (see L1).

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: (1) GVK 20/B: a 15% final bank withholding replaces income tax, with no books, no invoices and no KDV, for content creators, platform-based online services and app-store developers, up to TL 5.3m/yr (2026). (2) GVK 89/13: an 80% deduction on profit from listed services (software, design, engineering, data processing and others) exported to non-residents, provided the profit is brought into Türkiye. (3) GVK Mükerrer 20, young entrepreneurs: full taxpayers under 29 registering for the first time are exempt on business profit up to the 2nd-bracket amount (TL 400,000 in 2026) for 3 tax years. They must still file a return, and this cannot be combined with 20/B (per a 2022 tax ruling reported secondarily). (4) GVK 20/D (Law 7582, from 2026): people who become Turkish residents after 3 years with no Turkish domicile or tax liability get a 20-year exemption on foreign-source income. This is relevant to returning diaspora.

D1_id_document.question: Identity documents residents use for KYC (gateways, banks, platforms)
D1_id_document.answer: The chip-based Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Kimlik Kartı (TCKK), rolled out nationwide from 2 January 2017, is mandatory for every citizen. It carries the 11-digit T.C. kimlik numarası, which is also the tax ID (L2). A passport is the alternative for foreign platforms.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Physical or digital goods on Etsy (Etsy seller payments are available here). (6) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Fully localized'). (7) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
